Question: Consider the Cauchy problem
\[
 u_t(t,x)+\left(\frac{u^2(t,x)}{2}\right)_x={\bf N}[u(t,\cdot)](x),
 \qquad u(0,\cdot)=\bar u,
\]
on \([0,\infty)\times \mathbb{R}\), where \({\bf N}:H^1(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})\) is a bounded linear operator acting on the spatial profile \(u(t,\cdot)\). What is the strongest correct statement characterizing when this problem exhibits wave breaking (shock formation) at a time \(T^*>0\)?
Predicted label: 'E'
Predicted text: 'It exhibits wave breaking at time \\(T^*>0\\) precisely if the Cauchy problem admits a unique classical solution \\(u\\) on \\([0,T^*)\\times\\mathbb{R}\\) such that\n\\[\n\\limsup_{t\\to T^{*-}}\\left(\\inf_{x\\in\\mathbb{R}} u_x(t,x)\\right)=-\\infty.\n\\]'
Correct label: 'E'
Correct text: 'It exhibits wave breaking at time \\(T^*>0\\) precisely if the Cauchy problem admits a unique classical solution \\(u\\) on \\([0,T^*)\\times\\mathbb{R}\\) such that\n\\[\n\\limsup_{t\\to T^{*-}}\\left(\\inf_{x\\in\\mathbb{R}} u_x(t,x)\\right)=-\\infty.\n\\]'
Exact Match: 1.0
